title: Cohort-based batching profiler and safe recommendation apply
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a cohort-aware profiling and recommendation engine that suggests batching and caching configs per customer workload, plus a safe apply/rollback pipeline for automated config changes. The engine will group similar request cohorts, synthesize candidate batch parameters, simulate cost/latency trade-offs, and run a staged rollout (shadow -> canary -> gradual apply) with automated rollback triggers.
problem_statement: Current batching recommendations are one-size-fits-all and applied manually. This causes suboptimal unit cost for heterogeneous workloads, occasional tail-latency regressions after applies, and operational risk during mass updates. We need automated, cohort-specific suggestions plus a robust safety pipeline to apply them at scale.
goals: Produce per-cohort batching and prefix-caching recommendations (batch size, max latency target, KV cache TTL, coalescing window)
Expose a scoring function that estimates cost delta and tail-latency risk for each candidate
Implement a safe-apply workflow: shadow profiling, micro-canary, gradual ramp with rollback guards
Integrate with Console to show suggested config, impact estimate, and a 1-click apply (with audit trail)
non_goals: Replacing runtime's core scheduler — we produce recommendations and orchestrate apply, runtime changes are out of scope
Full automatic reconfiguration without human review for P0 customers
technical_design: Overview: The system has three logical pieces: (1) Cohortizer: groups requests by lightweight fingerprinting (model family, prompt token count distribution, request deadline SLA, customer tier, routing region), (2) Profiler & Simulator: for each cohort, synthesize request traces, run sampling through a local micro-bench runtime to measure latency/throughput and simulate coalescing and KV cache hit-rate changes, (3) Recommendation engine: generate candidate configs and score them by estimated cost savings vs tail-latency risk. Core heuristics: sequence-length aware batching (bucket into short/medium/long based on 90th percentile), deadline-aware batch cut (prefer smaller batches for low-deadline cohorts), cache-sensitivity score (if cohort shows high prefix-reuse, bias towards higher cache TTL and larger batch sizes), burstiness dampening (reduce batch target if short-term QPS spike variance > threshold), heterogeneity penalty (if single-host heterogeneity ratio > 0.25, limit max batch size to reduce serialization stalls). Scoring: each candidate gets a triple score: estimated unit-cost-savings (tokens/USD), P95 latency delta, and operational-risk score derived from divergence from baseline. Simulation: use weighted replay of recent windows (24h, 7d) and Monte Carlo draws for burst patterns. Apply workflow: 1) Publish recommendation to Console with explainability elements (why this cohort, simulated traces), 2) Shadow-apply mode where runtime accepts config but routes traffic to baseline; measure real-world divergence for 1h, 3) Canary apply to small slice (1-3% of traffic) for 30min with tight rollback checks, 4) Gradual ramp with exponential steps up to target with checkpoints. Rollback is automatic if any guard trips.
safety_checks: Canary window P95 latency > baseline P95 + 20% => immediate rollback
Token-per-request cost reduction estimate negative => block apply
Error-rate (500s) increase > 0.1 percentage points absolute => rollback
Observed KV cache hit-rate drop > 10% relative => revert cache TTL changes
Canary traffic should be pinned to healthy capacity nodes; if node OOM or GPU preemption events occur, rollback
Minimum shadow period: 1 hour or 1000 requests, whichever comes later
telemetry_requirements: Per-cohort P50/P95/P99 latency buckets pre/post apply
KV cache hit-rate and TTL distributions
Batch size distribution histogram (per model and per cohort)
Realized cost delta estimate (per-minute) vs simulation
Audit trail events for recommendation publish, shadow start, canary start, apply step, rollback
tasks: Spike: implement Cohortizer prototype and export cohort tags (ENG-841256-1)
Implement lightweight profiler + simulator that can run sample traces in CI (ENG-841256-2)
Recommendation engine: candidate generation and scoring (ENG-841256-3)
Console UI: show recommendations with explainability and 1-click safe-apply (ENG-841256-4)
Runtime hooks for shadow-apply and canary traffic allocation (infra change, coordinate with runtime team) (ENG-841256-5)
Safety runner: implement automated guards and rollback controller (ENG-841256-6)
Run pilot with three low-risk customers, collect metrics for two weeks (ENG-841256-8)
acceptance_criteria: System can produce cohort-level recommendations for 95% of active workloads without manual labels
Simulated estimates for pilot customers are within ±15% of observed cost delta after canary
Automated rollback triggers correctly revert canary changes in synthetic failure tests
Console displays recommendation, simulation traces, and audit events; a user can start a shadow run and a canary via the UI
Pilot customers see net unit-token cost reduction >= 10% with no >10% increase in P95 latency
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal-only Canary — run cohortizer and simulate recommendations, review dashboards (1 sprint). Phase 1: Shadow-only pilot for 3 customers (2 sprints). Phase 2: Canary ramp for pilot customers with automated rollback (2 sprints). Phase 3: Open beta for select self-serve customers with 1-click apply + enforced safety defaults (4 sprints). Phase 4: Gradual account-wide rollout with policy constraints and org-level opt-out (ongoing). Each phase must complete a runbook and postmortem before moving forward.
